children: Wheat for December delivery fell 2.4% to $7.28 3/4 a bushel on the Chicago Board of Trade Wednesday, in response to comments from a Russian official leaving the possibility open for peace talks between itself and Ukraine.
Corn for December delivery fell 1% to $5.28 1/4 a bushel.
Soybeans for November delivery fell 0.6% to $13.08 3/4 a bushel.

Change in Pace: Indications that Russia may be open to entering peace talks to mediate the 4-year Russia-Ukraine conflict pressed on CBOT wheat. "Wheat futures are facing increased selling pressure after a Russian official said there was a 'general political desire' to resume trilateral peace talks between Russia, Ukraine and the U.S. at some point in the 'foreseeable future,'" said Brian Grete of Commstock Investments. "Wheat remains sensitive to geopolitical headlines even as the attacks between Russia and Ukraine intensify."

Fleeing Their Posts: Fund traders hedged their bets ahead of Friday's WASDE report. "It's all money flow--buy the breaks, sell the rally," said Karl Setzer of Consus Ag Consulting. Wheat took the brunt of the selling, but all three row crops declined. Last week's Commitments of Traders report showed net long positions in wheat, corn, and soybeans--with corn and soybeans in particular having sizable net long positions, giving traders the room to trim their holdings in the event that the USDA doesn't move its forecasts as much as anticipated by analysts.

Shrinking Crop: Analysts surveyed by The Wall Street Journal forecast that U.S. corn yields will be pegged around 178.1 bushels per acre by the USDA, down 2.6 bpa from the USDA's projection in August. Soybean yields are seen at 52.5 bpa, which is down slightly from 52.7 bpa. Many private firms are forecasting lower production and yields for corn and soybeans, with corn in particular feeling the stress from hot and dry weather that struck in July and August.

Moving Volumes: The USDA announced a new round of flash sales, with 182,800 metric tons of corn sold to Mexico for delivery in the 2026/27 marketing year. Additionally, 340,000 tons of soybeans were sold for delivery to China in 2026/27. An additional 100,000 tons of soybeans were sold to unknown destinations for delivery in 2026/27. The round of sales is a positive demand indicator ahead of the USDA's WASDE Friday.

Off the Starting Line: This week's Crop Progress report from the USDA said that U.S. corn crops have started their harvest — with 5% of the crop harvested as of the week of Sept 6. That's one point higher than this time last year. The report does not show soybean harvesting as having started. Crop conditions for both corn and soybeans are steady, with corn in good-or-excellent condition down one point to 56%, while soybeans stay unchanged at 58% good-or-excellent. Harvesting usually begins around this time for U.S. corn, with soybean harvesting tending to start in October.
The EIA will release its Weekly Petroleum Status Update report at 10:30 a.m. ET Thursday.
The USDA will release its weekly export sales report at 8:30 a.m. ET Friday.
The CFTC will release its weekly Commitment of Traders report at 3:30 p.m. ET Friday.
